The issue might be that when `soft_wrap=True` is used, the background style is not correctly handled when the terminal wraps the text.

Wait, if `soft_wrap=True`, `rich` does NOT insert line breaks. It lets the terminal handle it.
If the terminal wraps the text, it doesn't know about the background style.
But `rich` should probably ensure that the background style is repeated at the beginning of the wrapped line if it can.
However, `rich` cannot know where the terminal will wrap the text unless it knows the terminal width.
But `Console` knows the terminal width.

Wait, if `soft_wrap=True`, `rich` just prints the whole string.
If the terminal wraps it, the background color will only be at the beginning of the first line (and end of the last line).
The lines in between will have no background color.

To fix this, `rich` could potentially insert the background style at the end of each line (where it would wrap) and at the beginning of the next line.
